items.title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pkg_resources' on Python 3.12
items.body:
---
### Description of issue

On Python 3.12, a fresh virtual environment (`venv`) no longer includes `setuptools` by default. `nipcbatt` still imports `pkg_resources`, which comes with `setuptools`, so the import fails unless `setuptools` is installed manually.

`pkg_resources` was also removed completely in **setuptools 82.0.0**. Installing the latest `setuptools` won't fix the error, so `setuptools` **<81.0.0** must be installed instead.

### Affected code

`src/nipcbatt/pcbatt_utilities/save_traces.py`:

```python
import pkg_resources
...
f.write("nipcbatt : " + pkg_resources.get_distribution("nipcbatt").version + "\n\n\n")
```

`setuptools` is only listed as a dev dependency in `pyproject.toml`, so a normal `pip install nipcbatt` doesn't install it.

### Symptoms

- `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pkg_resources'` when you import `nipcbatt.pcbatt_utilities.save_traces` or call `save_traces()`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a fresh Python 3.12 virtual environment: `python -m venv .venv`
2. Activate it and run `pip install nipcbatt`
3. Import or call `save_traces(...)`
4. You get `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pkg_resources'`

### Workaround

After you create and activate the virtual environment, install a compatible version of `setuptools` **<81.0.0** before installing the other dependencies:

```
python -m pip install "setuptools<81.0.0"
```

Then install `nipcbatt` as usual.

### Notes

- Use `setuptools` **<81.0.0**. Version 82.0.0 and later removed `pkg_resources`.
- Python 3.10 and 3.11 are usually not affected because their virtual environments still include `setuptools`. They can still break if `setuptools` is upgraded to 82.0.0 or later.
- Install `setuptools` before the other dependencies.

---

If the problem continues after you apply the workaround, please comment on this issue.

items.title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'breathe._parser' when installing from source
items.body:
## What happened

Installing Breathe from the repository source produces a package that any Sphinx project depending on it cannot load:

```bash
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'breathe._parser'
```

Minimal reproduction, using Breathe's own documentation build (48b3ca5c5f3e63248ae9e74359cc6bc604750a13 is the current `main`):

```bash
BRANCH=48b3ca5c5f3e63248ae9e74359cc6bc604750a13
git clone https://github.com/breathe-doc/breathe.git breathe
cd breathe
git checkout $BRANCH
conda create --prefix ./.venv --yes
conda activate ./.venv
export PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1
conda install python=3.14 doxygen=1.9.4 graphviz -c conda-forge --yes
python -m ensurepip
python -m pip install .[docs]   # build and install Breathe from source
make html
```

`make html` aborts while the Breathe extension is being loaded, and the extension is never registered at all:

```bash
Traceback
=========

      File ".../site-packages/breathe/parser.py", line 10, in <module>
        from breathe._parser import *
    ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'breathe._parser'
```

### The current workaround

[`documentation.yml`](https://github.com/breathe-doc/breathe/blob/48b3ca5c5f3e63248ae9e74359cc6bc604750a13/.github/workflows/documentation.yml#L60-L73) shows that CI currently works around this with a chain of steps:

```yaml
- name: Install Python dependencies
  run: |
    python -m pip install --upgrade pip
    python -m pip install --editable .[build]
    python -m pip install .[docs]
    python -m pip uninstall --yes breathe
- name: Build the documentation
  run: |
    make parser
    make html
```

What each step actually does:

1. `.[build]` / `.[docs]` : install the **dependencies** (`setuptools`, `jinja2`, `furo`, `sphinx-copybutton`, `sphinxcontrib-spelling`, ...).
2. `python -m pip uninstall --yes breathe` : remove the **Breathe package itself** that the previous commands just installed, so that Sphinx falls back to importing Breathe from the source tree.
3. `make parser` : generate `breathe/_parser.py` in the **source tree** by hand.

So it is a combination of "install the dependencies, tear the package itself out again, then manually add the generated file back".

### Why this shouldn't be the normal state

From a user's point of view, an editable or non-editable `pip install .[docs]` should be enough to run `make html`. In practice neither install method generates `breathe/_parser.py`:

```bash
# Editable install
python -m pip install --editable .[docs]

# Non-editable install
python -m pip install .[docs]
```

### Affected install methods

| How Breathe is installed | `breathe/_parser.py` present | Sphinx can build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pip install git+https://github.com/breathe-doc/breathe.git` | ❌ | ❌ |
| `git clone` + `pip install .` | ❌ | ❌ |
| `git clone` + `pip install -e .` | ❌ | ❌ |
| `pip install breathe` (PyPI wheel) | ✅ | ✅ |

The PyPI artifacts only work because [`create-release.yml`](https://github.com/breathe-doc/breathe/blob/48b3ca5c5f3e63248ae9e74359cc6bc604750a13/.github/workflows/create-release.yml#L56-L62) runs `make parser` by hand before `python -m build`.

```yaml
- name: Generate parser
  run: |
    make parser
    make format-parser
- name: Build distribution
  run: python -m build
```

As soon as that manual step goes away — or someone builds straight from a git tree — the problem reappears.

## Root Cause

`breathe/_parser.py` is a **generated** file, which is rendered from `xml_parser_generator/schema.json` and `xml_parser_generator/module_template.py.in` by `xml_parser_generator/make_parser.py`.

The [`CustomBuildPy`](https://github.com/breathe-doc/breathe/blob/48b3ca5c5f3e63248ae9e74359cc6bc604750a13/xml_parser_generator/setuptools_builder.py#L18-L41) hook responsible for generating it is written as a **setuptools** `build_py` subclass:

```python
# xml_parser_generator/setuptools_builder.py
from setuptools.command.build_py import build_py

class CustomBuildPy(build_py):
    ...
```

But Breathe's build backend is currently **flit**:

```toml
[build-system]
requires = ["flit_core>=3.7"]
build-backend = "flit_core.buildapi"
```

`flit_core` is deliberately minimal and **provides no extension point for custom `build_py` / `cmdclass` commands**. As a result, this hook is **never executed** during `pip install` or `python -m build`; it only runs when someone invokes [`make parser`](https://github.com/breathe-doc/breathe/blob/48b3ca5c5f3e63248ae9e74359cc6bc604750a13/Makefile#L21-L28):

```make
$(GENERATED_MOD): \
		xml_parser_generator/schema.json \
		xml_parser_generator/module_template.py.in \
		xml_parser_generator/make_parser.py
	python3 xml_parser_generator/setuptools_builder.py

.PHONY: parser
parser: $(GENERATED_MOD)
```

The conclusion: any install that follows the normal "build from source" path ends up without `breathe/_parser.py`, and CI can only paper over it with workarounds such as `make parser` and `pip uninstall breathe`.

## Proposed Solution

**_Migrate the build backend from flit to setuptools_**, so that the existing generation hook actually runs and the generated module is packaged with the distribution.

Theoratically, `pip install .` / `pip install -e .`, as well as installing from a git URL or a source archive, generate and package `breathe/_parser.py` during the build, and users no longer have to run `make parser` by hand.

items.title: Windows: server fails to start — ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'
items.body:
## Summary

The MCP server cannot start at all on Windows: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'`.

`fcntl` is imported at module level in two files, and both are reached on the import path of the server entry point, so this is not a lazy failure — `marketplaces_mcp.mcp_server.server` raises during import and the server never answers `tools/list`.

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "scripts/smoke-search.py", line 6, in <module>
    from marketplaces_mcp.mcp_server.server import marketplaces_search
  File "src/marketplaces_mcp/mcp_server/__init__.py", line 1, in <module>
    from .server import REQUIRED_TOOLS, mcp
  File "src/marketplaces_mcp/mcp_server/server.py", line 17, in <module>
    from marketplaces_mcp.core.ozon_tours_access import OzonToursAccess
  File "src/marketplaces_mcp/core/ozon_tours_access.py", line 5, in <module>
    import fcntl
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'
```

## Affected files

- `src/marketplaces_mcp/core/ozon_tours_access.py:5` — `import fcntl`
- `src/marketplaces_mcp/adapters/ozon_tours.py:7` — `import fcntl`

Both use `fcntl.flock(...)` for a lock file:

- `core/ozon_tours_access.py:81` inside `OzonToursAccess.status()`
- `adapters/ozon_tours.py:165` inside `OzonToursAdapter._lock()`

## The pattern already exists in this codebase

`adapters/avito.py` handles Windows correctly — it just was not applied to the Ozon tours modules:

```python
try:
    import fcntl
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - Windows
    fcntl = None

try:
    import msvcrt
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - POSIX
    msvcrt = None
```

with a guarded lock and a real Windows fallback via `msvcrt.locking(LK_LOCK / LK_UNLCK)`, wrapped in `if fcntl is not None:` / `if msvcrt is not None:`.

## Minimal reproduction

```
git clone https://github.com/YegorMy/marketplace-mcp.git
cd marketplace-mcp
uv sync
uv run python scripts/smoke-search.py --query "бумага a4" --limit 2
# ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'
```

Environment: Windows 10, Python 3.12.3 (MSC v.1938 64 bit), uv 0.12.15.

## Suggested fix

Apply the same `try/except ImportError` + `if fcntl is not None` guards as in `adapters/avito.py` to the two files above. Reusing the existing `msvcrt`-based lock helper would also preserve the cross-process mutual exclusion semantics that the lock file is there for (`OzonToursAccess` relies on `flock` returning `BlockingIOError` to report `probe_in_progress`, so a silent no-op changes behaviour under concurrent probes — worth deciding explicitly which is intended on Windows).

I verified locally that wrapping the import and guarding the two `flock` calls is enough to make the server start and complete a real search on Windows, so no other platform-specific code blocks startup.

## Two more Windows observations (lower priority, same session)

1. **6 tests fail on Windows** once the server starts, all on POSIX file-mode assertions:

```
FAILED tests/test_adapters_fixtures.py::test_avito_ip_block_starts_shared_cooldown
FAILED tests/test_adapters_fixtures.py::test_avito_state_path_can_live_under_existing_shared_directory
FAILED tests/test_avito_access.py::test_ip_and_challenge_have_distinct_reason_and_cooldown
FAILED tests/test_offer_regressions.py::test_busy_tour_lock_returns_structured_response
FAILED tests/test_tour_contracts.py::test_ozon_access_is_separate_from_search_and_cached_across_instances
```

Typical assertion: `assert path.stat().st_mode & 0o777 == 0o600` → `assert (33206 & 511) == 384`. Windows does not map `st_mode` to POSIX permission bits and ignores `0o600` in `os.open`/`mkstemp`, so these assertions cannot hold there. `test_busy_tour_lock_returns_structured_response` fails for a related reason: with no `flock` the busy-lock branch is not reached, and it gets a `ConnectError` status instead of `OZON_TOURS_PROBE_INTERRUPTED_OR_RUNNING`.

2. **`scripts/install-hermes-mcp.sh` is bash-only** (`BASH_SOURCE`, `command -v`). There is no `.bat`/`.ps1` equivalent, so the documented one-command Hermes setup cannot be used from a native Windows shell without git-bash/WSL. Adding the manual `mcp_servers` YAML block to the README (or a small Windows script) would cover it.

If a Windows CI job were added (none currently under `.github/workflows/`), the import failure in item 1 would be caught automatically on every push.

Happy to open a PR for the `fcntl` fix if that is useful — I have the working patch locally.

items.title: Crash on Windows: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl' (utils/single_instance.py)
items.body:
## Environment
- OS: Windows 11
- Python: 3.13.14
- codex-telegram: 0.6.0 (installed via pip)

## Description
`utils/single_instance.py` does `import fcntl` at module level, but `fcntl` does not exist on Windows. Since `bot/handlers.py` and `main.py` both import from `utils.single_instance` at module load, the bot crashes immediately on startup on Windows:

```
File ".../site-packages/bot/handlers.py", line 22, in <module>
    from utils.single_instance import find_local_conflict_candidates
File ".../site-packages/utils/single_instance.py", line 8, in <module>
    import fcntl
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'
```

## Suggested fix
1. Guard the import:
```python
try:
    import fcntl
except ImportError:  # Windows
    fcntl = None
```
2. In `SingleInstanceLock.acquire()` / `release()`, skip the `fcntl.flock` calls when `fcntl is None` (lock becomes best-effort on Windows, or use `msvcrt.locking`).
3. In `find_local_conflict_candidates()`, return `[]` when `fcntl is None`, it also iterates `/proc`, which does not exist on Windows.

I applied this patch locally and the bot now starts and runs fine on Windows (Codex app-server + Telegram polling OK). Happy to open a PR if wanted.
